Beállítom Az elmúlt tíz évben több mint 4,1 milliárd forint állami támogatást kapott a Kurultájt szervező Magyar-Turán Alapítvány – derül ki az RTL Híradó összesítéséből. A szervezet évről évre megrendezi a türk tudatú népek találkozójaként ismert eseményt, amelyre a korábbi Orbán-kormány rendszeresen biztosított közpénzt. A Fidesz szerint a támogatások a nemzeti identitás megőrzéséért végzett munkát ismerték el. Az alapítvány vezetője, Bíró András Zsolt a tíz év alatt több mint 4 milliárdos támogatás ellenére azt mondta egy sajtótájékoztatón, hogy a hozzájuk hasonló szervezetek kevés állami támogatásban részesülnek. Bíró az RTL Híradónak azt mondta, korábban a kulturális tárcával abban állapodtak meg, hogy a szervezet minden évben támogatást kap. Elmondása szerint később azt kérték tőlük, hogy tegyék átláthatóbbá a működésüket, aminek állítása szerint eleget is tettek. Bíró arról is beszélt, hogy a 2026-os támogatás nem érkezett meg Hankó Balázs minisztériumától, ezért személyesen Orbán Viktort kereste meg. Elmondta, hogy a volt miniszterelnök meghallgatta, azt ígérte, utánajár az ügynek, majd néhány héttel később megérkezett a 200 millió forintos utalás. Az ügyben két hete Tarr Zoltán is posztolt , a társadalmi kapcsolatokért és kultúráért felelős miniszter azt írta, hogy a választások után nem kevesebb, mint félmilliárd forintot osztott ki a Magyar-Turán Alapítványnak. „Minden támogatást kivizsgálunk, és szükség esetén megtesszük a jogi lépéseket is” – írta Tarr Zoltán a posztban. Photograph: Steven Saphore/AAP Australia news Three boys charged over alleged rape of teenage girl in Sydney home The 17-year-olds were charged over an alleged attack in Sydney’s south-west on Saturday Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australian Associated Press Wed 19 Aug 2026 20.05 EDT Last modified on Wed 19 Aug 2026 20.09 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Three teenage boys have been charged over the alleged rape of a 17-year-old girl at a home in Sydney’s south-west on Saturday. The three 17-year-old boys were arrested on Wednesday after the girl was allegedly attacked. New South Wales police searched several homes in the Macarthur region and seized electronic devices as part of their investigation, they said in a statement on Thursday. One of the boys has been charged with 11 offences, including six counts of aggravated sexual assault in company with others and three counts of rape, police said. Another of the boys was charged with six counts of sexual assault in company with others, rape and common assault. The third boy was charged with two counts of aggravated sexual assault in company with others. All three were kept in custody by police overnight and were due to appear in a children’s court on Thursday. https://www.dw.com/en/france-attack-rule.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MUIX An 18-year-old woman was seriously hurt in the accident Image: Guillaume Saligot/AFP Advertisement A train derailed on Friday evening between the cities of Rouen and Caen in Normandy, northwest France , authorities said. The public prosecutor of Rouen, Sebastian Gallois, said Saturday evening that there was "no indication of a malicious act carried out with the deliberate intention of derailing the train, and certainly not of an attack," according to reports in the French media. Gallois' remarks came after some politicians had suggested earlier on Saturday that the incident might have been the result of sabotage or other criminal activity. At least 44 people were injured in the accident, which occurred near the municipalities of Cleon and Tourville-la-Riviere at around 7:30 p.m. local time (18:30 UTC), the Seine-Maritime prefect said in a statement . One of ​the injured, a young woman, was in a critical state and was evacuated by helicopter to Rouen, the local authority added. Her condition has reportedly improved in the hours since. The train was carrying around 180 passengers when it derailed, national rail company SNCF and the prefect said. What else do we know about the train derailment? French Transport Minister Tabarot said 140 firefighters were at the scene. Local authorities had urged the public to avoid the area. The French rail network operator SNCF Reseau said traffic on the line had been suspended. "The priority is to care for the passengers and then to restore safe operating conditions," SNCF Reseau said. ​A police spokesperson had said the train derailed after hitting an unidentified object. A piece of rail that might have been involved has been found on the track, according to police reports. https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/crq5.text: Image source, AFP via Getty Images By Ian Aikman Â and Â Hugh Schofield ,Â Paris correspondent Published 12 October 2026 Hundreds of French supermarkets have been hit by a cyber attack that caused their fridges and freezers to heat up, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros. Hackers gained control of the software that regulates the temperatures of the refrigeration units, forcing some to warm to 50C (120F) overnight, according to one supermarket chain affected. The chief executive of CoopÃ©rative U said several of its supermarkets had been hit by the "extremely serious and unprecedented" attack. More than 100 of the chain's supermarkets were targeted, while 180 stores from IntermarchÃ© and its Netto brand were affected, with a spokesman saying that another 100 shops were urgently disconnected from the internet to prevent the same thing happening to them. Other major food retailers including Carrefour, Monoprix and E.Leclerc were also hit by the attack, which targeted software provided by Danish engineering firm Danfoss. The software allows retailers to manage their cold units remotely. Normally, supermarket freezers go through a short period of defrosting overnight, in which temperatures rise slightly. But the hackers ordered the units to heat up and stay hot, although Danfoss did not confirm any reports about just how warm the fridges and freezers could become in that process. Danfoss said the affected cold units were older models whose security software could not be updated to ward off a risk they had identified. The firm added in s statement that it had "long advised" businesses to keep supported systems up to date. "Reliable refrigeration is critical to our customers' operations, and we remain committed to supporting our customers and helping them maintain secure and reliable systems they are used to." The full scale of the attack is unclear, but figures supplied by individual chains suggest about 400 stores were affected out of 15,000 or so overall in France. Carrefour said fridges in 80 of its 6,000 stores were hacked, while Monoprix said 5% of its 400-plus stores had been hit, with food removed from sale if its condition could not be guaranteed. In a statement to the BBC, Mousquetaires Group - which owns IntermarchÃ© and Netto - said some fresh and frozen food display units remained out of service on Monday afternoon. The stores had "taken all necessary precautions to remove the products from these units", it said, adding that staff were working to restock the shelves "as soon as possible". IntermarchÃ© said its fridges had heated up to 50C for six hours overnight into Monday, and the retailer had thrown away all the affected food to avoid health risks, the Reuters news agency reported. As a result of the attack, managers arriving at branches of several supermarket chains on Monday morning were hit by a wave of hot air from the freezers. In some places there were even small fires. French broadcaster BFMTV published an image showing a freezer in an ice cream aisle displaying a temperature of 26.5C. Two supermarkets in the Alsace region reported losses of â¬270,000 (Â£228,000) between them, the broadcaster added, meaning the nationwide total could run into the millions. French prosecutors have opened a specific cyber-crime investigation into the incident, which the Paris prosecutor's office called a "large-scale cyber-attack affecting the refrigerators of several major food retail chains across France". European Food Commissioner Christophe Hansen condemned the hack in a post on X and added: "Food security requires more attention at all levels. Because the weaponisation of food has become a reality." In a post on X, CoopÃ©rative chief executive Dominique Schelcher said staff were "fully mobilised, in co-ordination with refrigeration specialists, to restore the situation as quickly as possible". He called for an investigation into the hack and said targeting equipment essential to the French food supply was "unacceptable". Have you been affected by this cyber attack? Share your experience . https://econotimes.com/NASA-Profile-Trac.text: Ground crews inspect an Artemis vehicle inside Kennedy Space Center's Vehicle Assembly Building in Florida. / EconoTimes.ai NASA's Oct. 16 profile follows Allison Mjoen's 20-year career at Kennedy from shuttle and space station work to Artemis vehicle operations for crewed lunar missions. NASA identifies Mjoen as its Exploration Ground Systems spacecraft offline operations manager. She watched Artemis II lift off with her children on April 1, 2026, the agency said. Her responsibilities include developing integration plans for Artemis vehicle processing and overseeing ground work involving booster and Orion spacecraft operations. She supports senior vehicle operations manager Matt Czech, according to NASA. Based at Kennedy, NASA's Exploration Ground Systems program runs the facilities and systems used to prepare Artemis rockets and spacecraft, conduct launches and recover vehicles. That work includes activity before launch and recovery after missions return to Earth. At United Space Alliance, Mjoen served as a flight crew systems engineer during the Space Shuttle Program. Her team planned cabin configurations for each mission, handling details that included food, spacesuits, cargo and payloads, NASA's profile says. She later became an International Space Station payload integration engineer. For Artemis I, she led the Spacecraft Payloads Integration and Evolution Element. NASA also says she served as a certified operations project engineer and supported integrated firing-room operations during that mission. NASA records show the Space Launch System lifted off from Kennedy's Launch Pad 39B at 6:35 p.m. ET (22:35 UTC) on April 1, 2026, with four astronauts aboard Orion. Artemis II completed a crewed lunar flyby and splashed down April 10. Its flight lasted nine days, one hour and 32 minutes. The mission did not include a lunar landing; NASA describes it as a step toward future lunar-surface missions. NASA's profile also points to the first Apollo Moon landing as a historical comparison for Artemis. Mjoen summed up her approach as “staying curious, working hard, building relationships.” She also said “our collective efforts directly contribute to the success of the mission.” NASA Kennedy Space Center Artemis II Orion Allison Mjoen Binance Loss Sharpens CFTC Chair’s Case for Optional Crypto Registration Rockwell Automation Sets Dec. 10 Payment for $1.45 Quarterly Dividend Heyman Says New Alaska Senate Report Prompted Law Enforcement Surge Mohawk Sets No Timetable for Its New $500 Million Share Buyback Trump Was Scheduled to Campaign for Republicans in Florida Science NASA Says Artemis II Shield Had Tenfold Lower Char Loss NASA counted nine char-loss spots on Artemis II’s heat shield, compared with 103 on Artemis I, and said postflight testing is continuing. https://www.g4media.ro/comisia-mykonos-d.text: Funcționăm ca organizație non-profit, iar banii rezultați din contribuțiile cititorilor sunt destinați integral finanțării proiectului G4Media. Comisia pentru Constituționalitate din Senat, condusă de senatoarea Cosmina Cerva (PSD, fostă SOS), nu a reușit să afle niciuna dintre circumstanțele în care judecătorul constituțional Cristian Deliorga a fost prezent în avionul privat care s-a deplasat pe 8 iulie în insula grecească Mykonos. Zborul a fost organizat de președintele Camerei de Comerț, Mihai Daraban, și la el au mai participat, printre alții, ministrul Muncii, Florin Manole, deputatul Victor Ponta, sau omul de afaceri Gruia Stoica. Principalul impediment pentru care comisia parlamentară nu și-a atins obectivele a fost faptul că judecătorul Cristian Deliorga a refuzat să se prezinte la audieri, în pofida numeroaselor invitații care i-au fost adresate. Comisia a reușit să constate, din lecturi ale presei, că există contradicții serioase între ceea ce declară Mihai Daraban și Cristian Deliorga: primul declară că se cunoaște cu Deliorag de peste 30 de ani, în timp ce cel de-al doilea susține că nici nu se cunoaște cu Daraban. În finalul raportului, Comisia constată că a fost în imposibilitate de a-și atinge vreunul din obiectivele pe care și le-a propus: circumstanțele participării lui Deliorga, cine i-a suportat deplasarea și eventualele beneficii materiale sau de altă natură pe care le-a primit. Comisia a decis să transmită raportul către Plenul Curții Constituționale, pentru a efectua propria anchetă și a stabili eventualele sancțiuni. Doamna e cumva distinsa senatoare pe care o pufnise rasul la tribuna Senatului cand isi anunta, mai acum vreo trei saptamani, transferul in interes de serviciu la PSD? Altfel, ideea de a muta anchetarea lui Deliorga la o comisie CCR – care probabil va fi condusa de Deliorga, pentru ca nimeni altcineva nu cunoaste mai bine cauza – mi se pare cat se poate de judicioasa si intrutotul consistenta cu modul in care functioneaza justitia romaneasca in vremea din urma. Asteptam cu sufletul la gura sa vedem daca Deliorga il va sanctiona ferm pe Deliorga. Traiasca PSD, rusine USR!!! Ne trebuie parlamentari serioși, parlamentul actual este o rușine națională!
